Read and clean the sheets of a Countdown 2030 workbook

Source: R/0_import_load_data.R
load_excel_parts.Rd

Reads and cleans each sheet of a Countdown 2030 Excel workbook and returns the sheets separately, without merging them. Use it to run data quality checks on each sheet before the merge, then pass the result to merge_and_standardize() to finish loading.

Usage

load_excel_parts(
  path,
  start_year = NULL,
  admin_sheet_name = NULL,
  population_sheet_name = NULL,
  reporting_sheet_name = NULL,
  service_sheet_names = NULL
)

Arguments

path

Path to an .xlsx or .xls file.

start_year

Optional integer filter for minimum year.

admin_sheet_name

Excel sheet with admin data. Default "Admin_data".

population_sheet_name

Excel sheet with population data. Default "Population_data".

reporting_sheet_name

Excel sheet with reporting completeness. Default "Reporting_completeness".

service_sheet_names

Character vector of service-data sheets. Default: all sheets matching "Service_data" if not supplied.

Value

A list with these elements:

  • parts: a named list of cleaned tibbles, one per sheet, named by sheet.

  • sheet_names: a character vector of the sheet names, in the order the sheets are merged.

  • sheet_ids: a named list of the key columns of the Admin sheet, the Population sheet and (as service_data) every other sheet.

  • admin_sheet_name, population_sheet_name, reporting_sheet_name, service_sheet_names: the sheet names used, with defaults filled in.

  • path, start_year: the arguments as given.

Details

Month names are standardized to English on every sheet that has a month column, and the original text is kept in a raw_month column. The sheets can then be joined on month even if they name the months in different languages.

The function stops with an error if a named sheet is not in the workbook, if a sheet is empty, or if a sheet lacks its key columns (district for the Admin sheet, district and year for the Population sheet, and district, year and month for the others). Other problems with the data are left to the data quality checks.

See also

merge_and_standardize(), run_all_quality_checks()

Examples

path <- system.file("extdata", "kenya.xlsx", package = "cd2030.core")
sheets <- load_excel_parts(path)
#> ℹ Loading Excel "kenya.xlsx" for parts
names(sheets$parts)
#> [1] "Service_data_1"         "Service_data_2"         "Service_data_3"        
#> [4] "Reporting_completeness" "Population_data"        "Admin_data"            
sheets$service_sheet_names
#> [1] "Service_data_1" "Service_data_2" "Service_data_3"
sheets$parts[[sheets$population_sheet_name]]
#> # A tibble: 235 × 9
#>    district         year pop_growth_rate total_population population_under_5ye…¹
#>    <chr>           <int>           <dbl>            <dbl>                  <dbl>
#>  1 Baringo          2019             3.2           733263                125574 
#>  2 Bomet            2019             2.7           963020                211064.
#>  3 Bungoma          2019             3.2          1837022                283060.
#>  4 Busia            2019             2.2           982892                154759 
#>  5 Elgeyo Marakwet  2019             3.5           499671                 86954.
#>  6 Embu             2019             1.4           669523                 74487.
#>  7 Garissa          2019             3.9          1012690                126501.
#>  8 Homa Bay         2019             2.6          1245362                194920 
#>  9 Isiolo           2019             2.5           292740                 32510.
#> 10 Kajiado          2019             3.6          1223577                159056.
#> # ℹ 225 more rows

#> #   total_births <dbl>, women_15_49_years <dbl>

# Month names are in English, the workbook's own text is kept beside them
unique(sheets$parts[[sheets$service_sheet_names[1]]][c("month", "raw_month")])
